title: Three layouts for auth.brickbot.ro
question: Same Arena Lights look as the website and linktree in all three: black, exact #FFEC17, Anek Latin, squircle boards. They differ in layout and in where the electric touch goes. Each sketch shows the sign-in screen at desktop size (open the expand chip for full size). The code, forgot-password, reset and invite screens follow the layout you pick. Lock one, or steer and re-roll.

options.label: Circuit Rail
options.lineage: the website's arc of current, turned upright into a circuit
options.thesis: Signing in is a short circuit: a vertical arc on the left links Sign in → Check your email → You're in, and current runs to the next node each time a step clears.
materials: vertical arc line with one zigzag
options.viewport: Logo and wordmark at top left; below them the upright rail with three steps, the first lit yellow. On the right, a surface board holds “Sign in”, the email and password fields, a full-width yellow “Sign in” button and “Forgot password?”.
options.risk: Three steps for a two-field form can feel like ceremony; the rail stays slim and is cut down to a one-line progress bar on phones.

options.label: Floodlit Split
options.lineage: the website hero: a floodlit competition photo with type where the scrim is
options.thesis: Half the screen is the team at Worlds under the arena floodlights; the other half is a quiet black desk with the form. A slim LED strip along the photo's bottom edge reports what's happening.
materials: outlined inputs that light yellow on focus
options.viewport: Left 55%: the Worlds practice-field photo, scrimmed only at the lower left where the wordmark and “Team access” sit, above an LED strip reading SIGN IN · MEMBERS ONLY. Right 45%: “Sign in”, two fields, the yellow button and the forgot-password link, vertically centred.
options.risk: The photo is the familiar split-screen login; it earns its place only if the LED strip does real work (code sent, wrong code, link expired).

options.label: LED Check-in
options.lineage: the linktree's centred column plus the LED perimeter board
options.thesis: One centred column, like links.brickbot.ro: the logo and wordmark on top, then an LED board that announces each step in lit dot-matrix type, then the form. The email code is typed into six LED digit cells.
materials: dot-matrix LED board as the step title
six LED digit cells for the code
options.viewport: Centred 440px column: logo mark over the wordmark; a full-width LED board reading SIGN IN with “members only” dim beside it; a surface board with email, password, the yellow button and “Forgot password?”; “Back to brickbot.ro” in the footer.
options.risk: Closest to the linktree, so the most cohesive and the least surprising; the LED board must stay readable and dim, not a gimmick.
